clue.text: Where it's about 66 degrees? It gets much colder there!

definitions.text: Where it's about 66 degrees? It gets much colder there!

parts.words: Where it's about 66 degrees? It gets much colder there!
parts.note: reads like a weather remark about a warm 66 degrees Fahrenheit, but the degrees are of latitude, marking the line beyond which the polar region begins

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on a mild 66-degree day and warns that it gets far colder somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests temperature in degrees Fahrenheit; the degrees are really latitude, about 66.5 degrees north, where the polar zone starts.
explanation.definitionFit: The line of latitude at roughly 66.5 degrees north bounds the frozen polar region, which is indeed much colder.

clue.text: Made journey and gasped audibly — taking rest here?

indicators.note: audibly says the words for the past journey and the gasp are to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: made a journey is rode, and gasped is sighed; said together they give the entry

explanation.surface: A traveller made a tiring trip, gasped for breath, and wonders where to stop for a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audibly' turns RODE and SIGHED, heard together, into the spelling of the entry; the definition is a place to pull over and rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A verge beside the highway is where a motorist might pull in and have a break.

clue.text: Check quality of river

definitions.meaning: to assess or try something out
the ..., a river flowing through Hampshire in southern England

explanation.surface: Someone is told to inspect the condition of a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: To try something out checks its quality; and the Test is a chalk-stream river in Hampshire, England, famous for trout fishing.

clue.text: Poet's talk on language cut by half

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the clue reads 'Poet is talk on language cut by half'

indicators.note: in a down clue 'on' places the second piece beneath, after the first

parts.note: chatter is idle talk

indicators.note: cut by half asks for only the front half of the word meaning language to be kept

parts.note: tongue is another word for a language

explanation.surface: A remark that a poet's chatter about language has been halved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut by half' keeps the first three letters, TON, of TONGUE; Thomas Chatterton was an 18th-century English poet who died at seventeen.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Chatterton was an English poet of the 1760s, known for his forged medieval verse.

clue.text: Some hint I mean to take before it's too late

definitions.text: to take before it's too late

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone drops a hint about something that should be taken before the deadline passes.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with time to spare means acting before the deadline, so the phrase fits taking a thing early.

clue.text: Trouser material all right in the wind

parts.note: chino is a cotton twill used for trousers
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Some cotton trousers are perfectly fine flapping in the breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: The chinook is a warm, dry wind that blows down the eastern side of the Rocky Mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinook is a warm dry wind descending the Rockies, so it is a named type of wind.

clue.text: Dec.'s binges — get fresh food

indicators.note: fresh suggests something made anew, so the letters are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: the abbreviation for December, with the possessive 's giving no letter

explanation.surface: December's festive overeating means it's time to get some proper fresh food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges DEC, BINGES and GET; the dish is poached eggs and ham on muffins topped with hollandaise sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: This brunch dish of poached eggs, ham and hollandaise on a muffin is a well-known item of cooking.

clue.text: Kingdom once undone by a crime

indicators.note: undone means taken apart, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An ancient realm was brought down by a single wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undone' rearranges A CRIME; Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercia was one of the Anglo-Saxon realms of early medieval England, now long gone.

clue.text: Huge Welsh girl meeting premature end

indicators.note: the girl's name is stopped short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Megan is a typical Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A big Welsh girl meets an untimely end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting premature end' cuts the last letter N from MEGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the prefix-turned-adjective means enormous or great, a slang synonym.

clue.text: Amazing jump by heather

parts.note: to start is to jump in surprise
ling is the common heather of moorland

explanation.surface: A surprising leap over a patch of heather.
explanation.walkthrough: LING is another name for common heather.
explanation.definitionFit: Something astonishing makes people jump, so it is surprising in the same sense.

clue.text: Something desirable for players musical or sporting?

definitions.text: Something desirable for players musical or sporting?

parts.words: Something desirable for players musical or sporting?
parts.note: musicians prize the ability to name any note by ear, while sportsmen want a flawless playing surface; one phrase serves both

explanation.surface: A question about what both musicians and athletes would most like to have.
explanation.walkthrough: For musicians it is the gift of identifying notes without reference; for cricketers or footballers it is an ideal playing surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a musician's ability to name notes unaided and an ideal sports ground, both things players want.

clue.text: Cut out physical activity without hesitation

indicators.note: without means the hesitation sound is removed from the longer word

parts.note: exercise is physical activity
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Advice to drop physical activity at once, with no dithering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes ER, the hesitation sound, from EXERCISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove by surgery or deletion is to excise, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A grave old doctor spells out a threat to humankind

parts.note: a tomb is a grave
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A solemn elderly physician casts spells that endanger the whole human race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like an adjective for the doctor but is the noun TOMB; 'spells out' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear weapon could wipe out civilisation, making it a danger to the human race.

clue.text: Audience two hours before midnight having a ball?

parts.note: ten o'clock at night, so at ten
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: An audience that turns up at ten at night to go to a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Two hours before midnight is ten o'clock, read as AT TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The number of people present at an event is its turnout, like an audience.

clue.text: Crooks in USSR — fat, red, drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests something staggering and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Soviet villains described as fat, communist and inebriated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges USSR, FAT and RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Swindlers who cheat people are crooks, the same idea of dishonest criminals.

clue.text: A monarch? No good getting close

indicators.note: no means the following letter for good is taken away

parts.note: a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A question whether a monarch who is no good is getting near.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes G (good) from KING to leave KIN; 'close' is the adjective meaning related or similar.
explanation.definitionFit: Being similar or related to something means being near to it in nature.

clue.text: Something to express denial, say, in the country

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for 'for example' inside the word for country

parts.note: a nation is a country
say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: A way of saying no, for instance, found throughout the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like a verb for expressing denial, but it is the usual crossword signal for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: A contradiction or refusal is a negative statement, a way of denying something.

clue.text: A saint buried in church container

indicators.note: buried in places the article and saint inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A saint's body lies interred inside a church vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buried in' puts A and S (saint) inside CE, the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A box or holder for storing things is a receptacle, such as a suitcase or display unit.

clue.text: Nut, alas, mistaken for fruit

indicators.note: mistaken suggests something got wrong, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A nut, sadly, has been confused with a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistaken' rearranges NUT and ALAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried seedless grape used in baking is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Tennis stroke — be at the front ahead of time

indicators.note: at the front means the little verb stands before the stroke

parts.note: a forehand is a tennis stroke

explanation.surface: Tennis advice: be at the net early with your forehand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tennis stroke' sits first in the clue, but its piece comes second in the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in advance means doing it earlier than needed, before time.

clue.text: Shrewd like trade union leaders with their employers

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: leaders asks for the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Being shrewd is compared to union chiefs negotiating with bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes the first letters of trade, union, their and employers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sharp and clever in judgement is perceptive, a synonym for shrewd.

clue.text: Covering doggie, say, at back of vehicle

indicators.note: at back of puts the animal piece after the vehicle piece

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a dog is an example of a pet

explanation.surface: A dog with a blanket over it in the back of the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering' is a noun here, a floor covering, not the verb it looks like at the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A rug or fitted floor fabric covers a floor, so it is a covering.

clue.text: A road flanked by parrots in trees

indicators.note: flanked by means the article and road sit with the parrot letters on either side

parts.note: Poll, from Polly, is a stock name for a parrot

explanation.surface: Parrots perch in trees on both sides of a road.
explanation.walkthrough: Poll, short for Polly, is the traditional name for a pet parrot; a pollarded tree has had its top branches cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: Trees whose upper branches have been cut back to encourage new growth are pollarded trees.

clue.text: Gum in fizzy drink imbibed by host

indicators.note: imbibed by means the drink is swallowed inside the host letters

parts.note: MC, master of ceremonies, is a host
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A host is drinking fizz with gum in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont in Italy; MC stands for master of ceremonies, who hosts an event.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastic is a resin from a Mediterranean tree, used as a chewing gum and adhesive.

clue.text: Manipulated? That's not new

definitions.meaning: exploited someone for one's own ends

explanation.surface: Someone suspects they have been exploited by something old.
explanation.definitionFit: Exploited someone for gain is one sense; second-hand, previously owned goods is the other.

clue.text: Harnesses needing fastening first to last

indicators.note: first to last means the opening letter is moved to the very end

parts.note: strapping is material used to fasten things

explanation.surface: Horse harnesses need their straps done up in order from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' moves the S of STRAPPING to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The ornamental harness of a horse is its trappings, as in a horse's tack and finery.

clue.text: Letter one's written with love and thanks

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I, with the 's giving no letter
love is zero in tennis, O
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A single letter written with love and gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is informal British for thanks; love is nil in tennis, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth character of the Greek alphabet is a letter.

clue.text: Distressing movement interrupting trial

indicators.note: interrupting means the movement word breaks into the middle of the trial word

parts.note: a hearing is a trial in court
a trend is a movement or tendency

explanation.surface: A protest movement disrupts an upsetting court trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trial' here is a court hearing, not a test, and 'movement' is a tendency rather than motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heartbreaking causes great sorrow, so it is distressing.
